title: Qualification sweep for E4M3 vs E5M2 quant profiles and activation circuit breaker
creator: Ethan Chen
description:
Goal: Safely enable customer-facing FP8 quantization profiles on Hopper-class hardware by running a qualification sweep comparing E4M3 and E5M2 profile behavior, and implement a low-latency activation circuit breaker (runaway-activation detector + rollback path).

Scope:
- Build a deterministic qualification harness that exercises model families (decoder-only and seq2seq) against the production request distribution (short, medium, long contexts).
- Run automated calibration permutations for candidate E4M3 and E5M2 scaling factors and capture accuracy deltas, per-op overflow signals, and KV-cache stability metrics.
- Define safety envelopes (max median perplexity delta, 99th-percentile token deviation, and tokenizer-level disagreement rate) and automatic abort/rollback triggers.
- Implement a fast-acting activation circuit breaker in the runtime control plane that can: mark a profile as degraded, disable new activations, shift traffic to INT8 or FP16 fallbacks, and schedule an automated re-check after cooldown.
- Add new telemetry and lightweight golden checks keyed to customer-visible prompts to detect silent regressions.

Success criteria:
1) Qualification sweep shows E4M3 or E5M2 candidate profile per model family with <= 2% median quality regression and no high-severity per-op overflows in production-like load.
2) Circuit breaker triggers within 30s of crossing configured threshold and rolls back activations with <0.5% increase in p95 latency.
3) Canary rollout automation can promote/demote profiles based on observed metrics without manual intervention.

Approach and deliverables:
- Calibration harness: a reproducible runner (k8s job) that executes N calibration seeds per profile variant and outputs a quality matrix, drift plots, and per-layer histograms. Deliverable: CI job and S3 artifact bundle.
- Qualification matrix: cross-model CSV with columns [model, profile, seed, median_ppl, tok_acc_drop, overflow_count, kv_inconsistency_rate]. Deliverable: stored in artifact store + HTML dashboard.
- Circuit breaker design: lightweight policy engine with rules: static thresholds, adaptive hysteresis, and emergency manual override. Deliverable: runtime PR (C++/Rust) + control-plane API + console UI toggle.
- Telemetry: new golden prompts, token-level divergence counters, and automated regression alerts in Ops. Deliverable: instrumentation + alert runbook.

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives from golden prompts: mitigate by using multiple diverse golden sets and requiring sustained signal across N samples.
- Calibration nondeterminism: add fixed RNG seeds and shadow-run comparisons.
- Latency/throughput impact from circuit-breaker checks: make checks asynchronous and off the hot path; only coordination messages on degradation.

Dependencies: see dependencies field.

Rolling plan: start with internal dedicated cluster canaries for 48h, then staged public canary across <1% traffic using runtime feature flags, then ramp with automated gates to 25% then 100% if no regressions and circuit breaker healthy.
